standard.title: Discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.description: use play, imagination, arts knowledge, processes and/or skills to discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior knowledge assumed. Students bring physical play, movement, and imaginative storytelling from everyday experience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use play, imagination and arts knowledge to discover movement possibilities and develop ideas for arts works.

nodes.label: Using play to discover movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use physical play and imagination to discover new ways of moving their bodies.
nodes.minimum_width: Structured play with movement prompts — exploring how body parts, levels, and bases can move safely and expressively.
nodes.typical_width: Open-ended movement exploration across multiple sessions: responding to imagery, music, emotions, or environmental features; discovering range across locomotor and non-locomotor movement.
wider: Use scarves, ribbons or other props to discover new movement possibilities and extend spatial awareness
Respond to contrasting music styles and tempos through movement — noticing how emotional response changes movement quality
nodes.hinge_reason: If students haven't developed physical play as a generative mode, they will be unable to self-generate movement ideas in the Creating strand — relying instead on imitation only.

response_modes.reason: Play-based movement discovery needs sustained time across varied prompts. Accumulating physical possibilities — different body parts, zones, directions — builds the store students draw on in Creating.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who play with movement across many different stimuli types develop a robust imaginative-physical connection that underpins creative work across all arts strands in later bands.
success_criteria: Student initiates new movement in response to a play-based prompt without direct imitation
Student explores at least two different ways of moving in response to the same stimulus

nodes.label: Developing and varying ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a movement idea further — varying, extending, or combining it — through imagination and play.
nodes.minimum_width: Taking one movement idea and extending or varying it in at least one way (e.g. doing it faster, bigger, at a different level, with a different body part).
nodes.typical_width: Using contrast and playful experimentation to extend movement ideas: changing level, direction, size, speed or body part; inventing new movements for familiar action songs; improvising rhythm patterns; responding to imagery with movement.
wider: Improvise movements that explain a process (e.g. steps in growing a plant), then develop a short sequence from these movements
Collaborate with peers to develop and extend each other's movement ideas through back-and-forth play

response_modes.reason: Varying ideas across different stimuli types — music, imagery, stories, games — builds transferable imaginative skill. Students who vary ideas in only one context remain dependent on that single prompt type.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who practise developing and varying movement ideas across diverse stimuli are better equipped to make intentional creative decisions in subsequent Creating and Presenting work.
success_criteria: Student can vary a movement they have made in at least one way when prompted
Student can show two different versions of the same idea
